name: Beef Chili Stuffed Acorn Squash with Cheddar & Green Onions

instructions.primary_message: Preheat oven to 260°C (500°F) and place rack in the center position. Line a large baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional).
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 acorn squash
1 ½ yellow bell peppers
3 sticks celery
1 small bunch green onions (scallions)

instructions.primary_message: Halve each acorn squash lengthwise, trim ends, and scrape out the seeds. Rub the inside of each half with oil, then season with salt and pepper. Arrange halves, cut-side down, on the baking sheet.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
¾ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Place squash in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until tender, so a knife can easily pierce through the flesh, about 25 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, trim, seed, and small dice bell peppers. Place in a small bowl.
Trim and small dice celery. Add to the bowl with the bell pepper.
Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.
While the pot heats up, trim and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces. Add half to the bowl. (Reserve remaining green onions for serving.)
Once the pot is hot, add veggies, beef, and spices. Cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 6-7 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
1.02 kg lean ground beef
3 tbsp chili powder
1 ½ tsp oregano, dried
1 ½ tsp salt
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Add tomato sauce and water to the pot. Stir to combine the chili and bring to a boil. Once boiling, reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, 10-12 minutes. Remove from heat.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 (213 ml) cans tomato sauce
¾ cup water

instructions.primary_message: To serve, divide squash halves between plates and fill with the chili; top with cheese and reserved green onions. Enjoy!
